newsitem.title: INDIA: India unhappy with WTO trade, investment groups.
newsitem.headline: India unhappy with WTO trade, investment groups.

text.p: India said on Friday it was unhappy with a decision by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on investment and trade competition, but said it had won a key battle over international labour standards.

"I think barring some unhappiness about the reference to two working groups on trade and investment, our brief has been faithfully adhered to by our delegation," Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told the lower house of parliament.

Chidambaram said India had opposed a decision by some developing countries to accept the working groups despite those nations' earlier opposition to any mention of the Multilateral Agreement on Investment, strongly favoured by the United States.
He said while reluctantly agreeing to the two groups, India had put forward two riders which were accepted by the WTO.

He said the riders stipulated that "the work that will be done by the working groups shall not pre-judge the question whether negotiations will be initiated at all...(and) any decision on future negotiations will take place only after an explicit consensus decision among the WTO members".
Chidambaram promised to hold a full discussion on the issue in parliament on Monday. Earlier, opposition and ruling party deputies slammed the agreement as a "sellout" of the country's sovereignty.
